title: Admin - Edit Admin Permissions - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Edit Admin Permissions feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Super Admins to click 'Edit Permissions' on an admin card to open a permissions editor with pre-selected existing permissions, add/remove permissions via checkboxes, and save changes that reflect immediately on the admin card. Edge cases include preventing save when all permissions are removed and resetting to old permissions on update failure. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for button accessibility, permissions editor (modal/panel), checkbox interactions, validation, error handling, and dynamic content updates.

testCases.title: Edit Permissions button has accessible name with admin context
testCases.componentElement: Edit Permissions button on admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Internal Administrators page is loaded with at least one admin card
steps: Navigate to an admin card's 'Edit Permissions' button using screen reader
Verify the button has an accessible name that includes context (e.g., 'Edit Permissions for John Doe')
Verify the button role is announced
If multiple admin cards exist, verify each button is distinguishable
expectedResults: Button has accessible name that identifies which admin's permissions will be edited
Screen reader announces 'Edit Permissions for [Admin Name], button' or similar
If multiple Edit Permissions buttons exist, each is uniquely identifiable (via aria-label or aria-describedby)
Button role is correctly announced
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users can identify which admin's permissions they are editing

testCases.title: Edit Permissions button is keyboard accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Tab to the 'Edit Permissions' button on an admin card
Verify the button receives visible focus
Press Enter to activate the button
Verify the permissions editor opens
Close the editor, return to button, press Space
Verify the permissions editor opens again
expectedResults: Button is reachable via Tab key
Visible focus indicator appears with at least 3:1 contrast
Enter key opens the permissions editor
Space key also opens the permissions editor
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: Edit Permissions button is fully keyboard accessible

testCases.title: Permissions editor has proper dialog/panel role and accessible name
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, 'Edit Permissions' button has been activated
steps: Click/activate 'Edit Permissions' button
Verify the editor has role='dialog' (if modal) or appropriate landmark role (if inline panel)
Verify the editor has an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby)
Verify screen reader announces the editor context on open
If modal: verify aria-modal='true' is set
expectedResults: Editor has role='dialog' or is a clearly identified region
Accessible name includes context (e.g., 'Edit Permissions for John Doe')
Screen reader announces the editor name and role on open
If modal: aria-modal='true' is present and background is inert
testCases.postconditions: Permissions editor is properly identified by assistive technologies

testCases.title: Focus moves to permissions editor on open
testCases.componentElement: Permissions editor focus management on open
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, about to open permissions editor
steps: Activate the 'Edit Permissions' button
Observe where keyboard focus moves when the editor opens
Verify focus is placed on the first focusable element in the editor (close button, heading, or first checkbox)
Verify focus does not remain on the trigger button
expectedResults: Focus moves into the permissions editor immediately upon opening
Focus is placed on the first focusable element
Focus is not left on the background page
Screen reader announces the editor context
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly managed when editor opens

testCases.title: Existing permissions are pre-selected and announced
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open for an admin with existing permissions
steps: Open the permissions editor for an admin who has some permissions assigned
Navigate through the permission checkboxes using screen reader
Verify pre-selected permissions are announced as 'checked'
Verify unassigned permissions are announced as 'not checked'
Verify the visual state matches the announced state
expectedResults: Previously assigned permissions have checkboxes in 'checked' state
Screen reader announces 'checked' for pre-selected permissions
Screen reader announces 'not checked' for unassigned permissions
Visual checkmarks match the programmatic state
All permissions are correctly pre-populated
testCases.postconditions: Existing permissions are accurately reflected in the editor

testCases.title: Permission checkboxes are operable via keyboard
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open
steps: Tab to the first permission checkbox in the editor
Press Space to toggle the checkbox (check if unchecked, uncheck if checked)
Verify the state changes
Tab to the next checkbox and toggle it
Repeat for all permission checkboxes
expectedResults: Each checkbox is reachable via Tab key
Space key toggles the checked/unchecked state
State change is visually indicated immediately
Screen reader announces the new state ('checked' or 'not checked')
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: All permission checkboxes are keyboard operable

testCases.title: Permission checkboxes have accessible labels
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open
steps: Navigate to each permission checkbox using screen reader
Verify each has a programmatically associated label
Verify labels match the permission names (User Management, Vendor Management, etc.)
Verify clicking/tapping the label text toggles the checkbox
expectedResults: Each checkbox has a programmatically associated label (via <label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
Screen reader announces the permission name with each checkbox
Labels are descriptive and unique
Label click toggles the associated checkbox
testCases.postconditions: All checkboxes are properly labeled

testCases.title: Permissions editor traps focus (if modal)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open as a modal
steps: With the editor open, press Tab repeatedly
Verify focus cycles through all interactive elements within the editor
When focus reaches the last element (Save button), press Tab
Verify focus wraps to the first element in the editor
Press Shift+Tab from the first element
Verify focus wraps to the last element
expectedResults: Focus cycles through: close button → checkboxes → Save button (and back)
Focus wraps from last to first on Tab
Focus wraps from first to last on Shift+Tab
Focus never escapes to background page while editor is open
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly trapped within the modal editor

testCases.title: Escape key closes the permissions editor without saving
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open with changes made
steps: Open the permissions editor
Make changes to some checkboxes (add/remove permissions)
Press Escape key
Verify the editor closes
Verify focus returns to the 'Edit Permissions' button
Verify changes are NOT saved (permissions remain as before)
expectedResults: Escape key closes the editor
Focus returns to the 'Edit Permissions' trigger button
No changes are saved (permissions revert to original state)
Admin card still shows the original permissions
testCases.postconditions: Editor can be dismissed without saving via keyboard

testCases.title: Focus returns to Edit Permissions button when editor closes
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open
steps: Close the editor using the close button (X)
Verify focus returns to the 'Edit Permissions' button
Open editor again, close with Escape
Verify focus returns to the 'Edit Permissions' button
Open editor, save changes
Verify focus returns to an appropriate element
expectedResults: After close button: focus returns to 'Edit Permissions' button
After Escape: focus returns to 'Edit Permissions' button
After successful save: focus returns to trigger button or updated admin card
Focus is never lost to the top of the page
testCases.postconditions: Focus is properly restored after editor closes

testCases.title: Save button has accessible name and keyboard activation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open with at least one permission selected
steps: Tab to the Save button in the permissions editor
Verify the button has a visible focus indicator
Verify screen reader announces 'Save, button' or 'Save Permissions, button'
Press Enter to save
Verify permissions are saved
Reopen editor, press Space on Save button
Verify permissions are saved
expectedResults: Save button is reachable via Tab
Visible focus indicator appears
Screen reader announces button name and role
Enter key saves permissions
Space key also saves permissions
Permissions update immediately after save
testCases.postconditions: Save button is fully accessible

testCases.title: Save is disabled/prevented when all permissions are removed
testCases.componentElement: Save button disabled state / validation error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open
steps: Uncheck all permission checkboxes
Observe the Save button state
If Save is disabled: verify aria-disabled='true' and screen reader announces 'disabled'
If Save shows error on click: verify error message is accessible
Verify an error/instruction message explains why save is not allowed
expectedResults: Save button is disabled (aria-disabled='true') OR clicking shows an accessible error
Screen reader announces the disabled state or error message
Error/instruction clearly states 'At least one permission must be selected'
Error is programmatically associated with the permissions group or announced via aria-live
User understands why they cannot save
testCases.postconditions: Users are clearly informed that at least one permission is required

testCases.title: Permission update failure resets to old permissions with accessible notification
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open, backend is configured to fail on save
steps: Make changes to permissions (add/remove some)
Click Save (with backend failure simulated)
Verify an error notification is displayed
Verify the error uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
Verify screen reader immediately announces the error
Verify checkboxes reset to the original (old) permissions state
expectedResults: Error notification is visually displayed (e.g., 'Failed to update permissions. Reverting to previous settings.')
Screen reader immediately announces the error
Checkboxes revert to the original pre-edit state
Error does not rely solely on color
Error text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
User can retry the action
testCases.postconditions: Failure is communicated and state is consistent (reverted)

testCases.title: Successful permission save is announced accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions editor is open with valid changes
steps: Make changes to permissions
Click Save
Verify a success message is displayed or announced
Verify screen reader announces the success
Verify the editor closes (or indicates save complete)
Verify the admin card reflects updated permissions
expectedResults: Success is communicated via toast/notification with role='status' or aria-live='polite'
Screen reader announces success (e.g., 'Permissions updated successfully')
Editor closes after successful save
Focus returns to appropriate element
Admin card shows updated permissions
testCases.postconditions: Successful save is communicated to all users

Verify the updated permissions are displayed visually

Verify screen reader announces the updated permissions with a label
Verify the change is reflected immediately without page refresh
expectedResults: Updated permissions are visually displayed on the admin card
Permissions have a descriptive label (e.g., 'Assigned Permissions')
Screen reader announces the updated permission values
Change is reflected immediately (dynamic update)
Permissions text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
testCases.postconditions: Updated permissions are accessible on the admin card

testCases.title: No keyboard trap in permissions editor

expectedResults: If modal: focus is contained but Escape provides exit (not a trap)

steps: Measure the clickable/tappable area of each permission checkbox (including label)
Verify adequate spacing between checkboxes

expectedResults: Each checkbox + label has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
